subject: Post-call: Model evaluation recommendations & stability decision ladder
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@acmedigital.com>; Tara Li <tara.li@acmedigital.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Model evaluation recommendations & stability decision ladder

Hi Sam / Tara —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan. High-level takeaways from the discovery call:

- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference for ACME's customer support summarization pipeline with strict precision on extracted action items and no regressions to recent accuracy baselines.
- Current pain: production uplift in F1 on summaries flagged earlier this quarter after model updates; you cited a ~7% drop on the key action-item extraction slice.
- Constraints: 95th percentile latency target <= 150ms, data residency in US, and ability to freeze model version if we see quality regressions.

Recommended immediate steps (short timeline):
1) Evaluation pack (attached) — we prepared a focused eval with your sample set plus an expanded slice of 2k representative conversations. Includes the prompt set we discussed (prompt_set_acme.xlsx) and benchmark scripts.
2) Baseline suggestion — run A/B of rdlw-v3.0 (current prod) vs rdlw-v3.2 (latest) across the ACME slice. We recommend the stability ladder below to govern decision-making.
3) Stability decision ladder (high level):
   - If delta(F1_action_items) <= 1.5% (v3.2 vs v3.0): proceed with gradual rollout and continuous monitoring.
   - If 1.5% < delta <= 4%: hold rollout, create pin to v3.0 for production, run targeted prompt tuning & eval (5 business days).
   - If delta > 4% or safety drift observed: immediate rollback to pinned version + postmortem and coordinated remediation plan.

Attachments included: acme_eval_pack_v2.zip (benchmarks + sample harness), prompt_set_acme.xlsx, diff_snapshot_v2_vs_v3.json (quick diff highlights).

Ask: Can you confirm we have permission to run the ACME test harness on your anonymized slice and that Tara can upload the additional 250 edge-case transcripts to the shared Drive link? Also confirm your preferred downtime window if we need to pin/roll back.

I'll coordinate with Marissa and Aditya on timelines and will stand up the eval cluster once you give the go-ahead. Proposed checkpoint: 48 hours after we share the first eval results.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

---
From: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@acmedigital.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Li <tara.li@acmedigital.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model evaluation recommendations & stability decision ladder

Connor —

Appreciate the succinct recap. Yes, you captured the call correctly. A few clarifications and immediate asks from our side:

- We can grant access to an anonymized slice. Tara will upload the additional 250 transcripts by EOD tomorrow.
- The regression numbers I mentioned are from our internal sampling: since v3.2 rolled out two weeks ago, we see a 6.9% drop on the action-item F1 specifically for long, multi-turn threads (>= 12 turns).
- We have one concrete failing example I pasted below (sanitized). That case turned a 3-line action item into three unrelated bullets after the update, which is a production blocker for us.

--- forwarded message ---
From: QA Bot <qa+failures@acmedigital.com>
Date: 2027-04-03 10:24:12 -0700
Subject: sample-fail-ACME-2398

Conversation snippet (sanitized):
[...conversation omitted...]
Expected action items:
- Contact billing to confirm seat count
- Schedule migration window (2-3 hours)
Actual (v3.2):
- Reach out about billing
- Review migration
- Follow up on unrelated marketing ask

---

Given that delta, the decision ladder you proposed makes sense. One ask: if we do pin to v3.0, can you share the estimated cost delta for running v3.0 pinned (per 100k tokens/day) vs trying a staged rollout with shadowing? We need that for our procurement decision.

Thanks,
Sam Brooks
Head of Product, Acme Digital
sam.brooks@acmedigital.com

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@acmedigital.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model evaluation recommendations & stability decision ladder

Sam / Connor —

Thanks for the example, Sam. That's exactly the type of regression we want the eval to catch. Concrete operational plan and short answers below.

Operational plan (48–120 hour window):
1) Intake & harness run (48 hrs): Tara uploads transcripts -> we ingest and run the eval suite. We will generate per-slice metrics and produce the artifact acme_eval_results_v1.html in the Drive folder.
2) If reproduction of the ~6.9% drop is confirmed: we will immediately create a temporary pin to rdlw-v3.0 for your production traffic. Pin duration proposal: up to 10 business days while we run mitigations (prompt adjustments, targeted fine-tune testing, and roll-forward tests).
3) Parallel remediation (3–10 days): ad-hoc prompt tuning + curated prompt_set_acme.xlsx adjustments; run small-scale candidate variants (v3.2-p1) in canary at 5% traffic.
4) Decision & rollback: if canary fails or new deltas appear > 2% on held slices, full rollback remains the default.

Cost notes: estimated incremental cost to pin rdlw-v3.0 vs rolling forward is modest relative to model token cost; rough estimate: pinned v3.0 adds ~12% per-token compute differential vs v3.2 at current billed rates (we'll produce exact numbers in the eval report). Shadowing (no pin) increases cost ~8% due to duplicate inference calls but avoids version freeze risk. We'll include a cost table in acme_eval_results_v1.html.

Permissions / compliance: we will only run the eval on anonymized transcripts; audit logs will be provided. If ACME requires a formal Data Processing Addendum, Connor and I can route that to your legal team.

Next steps: Connor will kick off the eval once Tara uploads. Can we schedule a 30-minute checkpoint on Monday (2027-04-05) at 10:00 PT to review initial metrics? If that's ok, I'll block it.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: acme_eval_pack_v2.zip (benchmarks + harness)
Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-eval-pack

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@acmedigital.com>, Tara Li <tara.li@acmedigital.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model evaluation recommendations & stability decision ladder — checkpoint scheduled

Sam / Tara —

Thanks — Tara, once your upload completes I'll start the ingest and run. I confirmed the Drive folder permissions with Marissa and dropped the eval harness there.

Confirming the meeting: Monday 2027-04-05 10:00 PT works for us (I've added the calendar invite). Agenda for the 30-min checkpoint:
- Quick readout of per-slice deltas (action-item F1 + precision/recall)
- Review any obvious failure modes (we'll highlight 3 canonical failures)
- Recommendation: pin vs canary + cost delta summary

If the run reproduces the ~7% drop on the long-thread slice, our proposed immediate action will be: temporary pin to rdlw-v3.0, run targeted prompt adjustments (2–3 business days), then canary v3.2-p1 at 5% traffic. We'll share the exact cost delta table in the first deliverable.

Deliverables you'll receive within 48 hrs after ingest: acme_eval_results_v1.html (drive link), per-case CSV of failing examples, and a short README with recommended prompt edits.

Please reply if you'd prefer a different checkpoint time. Otherwise we'll proceed as planned.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Attachments: prompt_set_acme.xlsx, diff_snapshot_v2_vs_v3.json
